 Trump ‘loves the guy’: Sergio Gor tipped for major promotion after midterm results: Report
 The reported discussions come amid speculation over possible changes in the Trump administration during the second half of his presidential term
 By ANI 
 Updated - November 05, 2026 at 09:19 AM. 
 | 
 Washington
 × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/trump-loves-the-guy-sergio-gor-tipped-for-major-promotion-after-midterm-results-report/article71668551.ece Copy 
 FILE PHOTO: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has dismissed reports suggesting he is interested in a senior position in the Trump administration.
 | Photo Credit:
 KEVIN LAMARQUE
 As political circles in Washington DC recalibrate after Republicans endured a midterms thrashing on Tuesday night, attention has increasingly turned towards potential administration shifts, with United States Ambassador to India Sergio Gor emerging in internal discussions as a contender for a senior promotion, according to a report by The Washington Sun citing multiple individuals familiar with the matter.
 Gor reportedly considered for senior administration roles
 Gor, who previously served as a senior White House aide and maintains close ties to President Donald Trump, was reported as having been been laying the groundwork for an expanded role following the midterms, according to ten sources familiar with internal discussions.
 According to sources cited by The Washington Sun, Gor has been mentioned in presidential circles as a candidate for senior administrative roles during the second half of the presidential term. There is reportedly a widespread understanding among State Department personnel that Gor harbours an interest in securing a more prominent assignment.
 “He wants more of a forward-facing role,” stated a US official familiar with internal discussions, as reported by The Washington Sun.
 White House Chief of Staff, Secretary of State roles discussed
 Individuals familiar with the situation indicated to the publication that Gor’s name has circulated as a possibility for influential positions, including White House Chief of Staff or successor to Secretary Rubio. Additional sources suggested to The Washington Sun that Gor might also consider alternative State Department elevations, such as succeeding Deputy Secretary Chris Landau.
 Gor and White House reject speculation
 Both Gor and administration representatives strongly rejected the circulation of such reports.
 In a statement provided to The Washington Sun, Gor dismissed the speculation entirely, saying, “This story is complete and total bullshit,” adding, “Secretary Marco Rubio has proven to be the most qualified, accomplished and greatest secretary of state in history. He is irreplaceable, and a dear friend who I have the joy of working with every day as US ambassador to India, a true honour of a lifetime. I have zero interest in any other role.”
 A White House official likewise dismissed the report as fabricated, stating that Gor harbours no interest in alternative positions.
